question: Which of the following monument is built with some influence of Gujarati style to welcome King George V and Queen Mary to India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (12/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: Jallianwala Bagh
Sun Temple
India Gate
Gateway of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Gateway of India

Explanation:
The Gateway of India is a famous monument located in Mumbai, built in 1911 to welcome King George V and Queen Mary to India. Its design was prepared by architect George Wittet and clearly shows influence of Gujarati style. The monument is made of basalt stone and stands 26 meters high. Construction was completed in 1924. The Gateway of India is also a significant symbol of India's independence movement, as the last British troops left India through this route in 1947.

question: When did Sir William Jones found Asiatic Society? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (12/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: 1793
1784
1854
1782
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1784

Explanation:
Sir William Jones, a renowned British philologist and jurist, founded the Asiatic Society on January 15, 1784 in Calcutta. The society aimed to study Asian culture, history, and languages. It later became known as the Asiatic Society of Bengal. Jones played a key role in translating ancient Indian texts and introducing Sanskrit to the Western world. He proposed that Sanskrit, Greek, and Latin shared a common origin, laying the foundation for the Indo-European language family theory. The establishment of the Asiatic Society marked the beginning of systematic Oriental studies in India.

question: Who among the following freedom fighters was NOT involved in the Kakori Train Robbery? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (12/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: Chandrashekhar Azad

Explanation:
The Kakori Train Robbery took place on 9 August 1925. This incident involved Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Chandrashekhar Azad and other revolutionaries. question: When did Moplah revolt (Malabar Rebellion) in Kerala take place? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (12/01/2021) Shift 1)

solution:

Explanation:

The revolt was also linked to the Khilafat Movement. The leaders of this revolt were Ali Musliyar and Varyam Kununnathu Haji. Several clashes occurred during the revolt, and the British army brutally suppressed it. This is an important chapter in the Indian freedom struggle.

question: Who described the kingdom of Awadh as 'a cherry that will drop into our mouth one day'? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (13/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: Lord Wellesley

Lord Curzon
Lord Henry Hardinge
solution:

Explanation:

He described the kingdom of Awadh as "a cherry that will drop into our mouth one day", implying its annexation was inevitable soon. In 1856, Awadh was annexed on the grounds of misgovernance. This statement reflects Dalhousie's expansionist policy and his desire to bring fertile Awadh under British control, which later became a major cause of the 1857 Revolt.

question: Which of the following banks was established in India at Calcutta under European Management (in 1770)? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (13/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: Indus Bank of India
Bank of Hindustan
National Bank of India
Bank of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Bank of Hindustan

Explanation:
Bank of Hindustan was the first bank in India, established in 1770 in Calcutta (now Kolkata) under European management. It was founded by employees of the British East India Company. This bank ceased operations in 1832. Later, banks like Bank of Bengal (1809) and Bank of Bombay (1840) were established. Indus Bank of India and National Bank of India were founded later. Bank of India was established in 1906. Therefore, the bank established in 1770 in Calcutta is Bank of Hindustan.

question: In which year did the East India Company acquire 'Diwani' rights over Bengal and Bihar? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (16/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: 1865
1765
1675
1965
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1765

Explanation:
The East India Company acquired the Diwani rights over Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha in 1765 from the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II. This right was obtained after the Battle of Buxar (1764), where the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah, and Shah Alam II were defeated. Diwani meant the right to collect revenue. With this, the Company became the de facto ruler of Bengal. This event is considered the foundation of British rule in India. The rights were granted under the Treaty of Allahabad in 1765, giving the Company control over Bengal's revenues.
